correctness.rationale: Block criterion T regular iff im D subset im B is proved both directions, then the stabilizer-preserving shear conjugates T to diag(B,0). This gives exactly one stabilizer orbit per nilpotent B type λ, ambient λ plus c zero blocks, rank r−ell(λ), and index λ1. D columns each independently lie in im B, giving q^{c rank B} lifts; the classical finite-field nilpotent orbit centralizer yields the exact Nλ. Summing over λ and applying the standard total q^{r²−r} proves the proportion; unique maximal-rank partition (r) yields the asymptotic with r=1 boundary. Powers show the sharp index r+1 for nonregular maps when c>0. Actual saved checker independently enumerates all matrix maps in nine small prime-field parameter triples and directly searches TUT=T for one case.

originality.rationale: Inspected the closely matching structural full texts: Grau establishes Q via image equality and studies Green/ideal structure; Sommanee--Sangkhanan computes maximal regular subsemigroups and generating ranks. Neither of their inspected theorems gives the nilpotent Jordan-type orbit counts, rank/index enumerator, or codimension decay. Earlier Sullivan and Nenthein--Kemprasit characterize related structure/regularity, so their contributions are not re-claimed. Actual semantic result searches recovered only distinct Jordan-lift/dual-number and general nilpotent problems; these do not imply the stated restricted-range regular-stratum formula. Residual risks about earlier equivalent enumeration remain.

value.rationale: The regular locus Q is a natural maximal regular subsemigroup of the restricted-range transformation semigroup studied in primary literature. The theorem supplies its complete nilpotent Jordan-orbit and joint matrix-rank/nilpotency-index distribution over all finite fields, not a narrow arbitrary slice. The structural shear normal form also separates the sharp maximal index for regular from nonregular nilpotents, while exact codimension decay quantifies the thinning of regular nilpotents as ambient dimension grows. None of the displayed outcomes is just a known matrix nilpotent count or generating-rank recomputation.
